tips.title: G190/G191 diameter vs radius mode switching
tips.body: G190 selects radius mode (X values = distance from centerline), G191 selects diameter mode (X values = full diameter). Diameter mode is standard for turning as it matches blueprint callouts. Some posts output G190/G191 explicitly; others assume diameter mode. Verify your post matches your controller expectation.

tips.title: Tttww tool and wear offset encoding
tips.body: Lathe T-word format: Tttww where tt=tool station (01-99), ww=wear offset register (00-99). Example: T0101 = tool 1, wear offset 1. T0102 = tool 1, wear offset 2. Multiple wear offsets per tool allows tight tolerance control on separate features — rough with one offset, finish with another to compensate tool wear.

tips.title: Automatic chamfer with C-word on lathe
tips.body: Program C±value after a single-axis G01 move to add a 45° chamfer. Value = chamfer leg length. Sign depends on direction: X+ moving toward Z- uses C-; X- moving toward Z+ uses C+. Requires single-axis move before chamfer (not diagonal). Example: G01 X1.0 C-0.030 Z-2.0 adds 0.030" chamfer.

tips.title: Automatic corner radius with R-word on lathe
tips.body: Program R±value after a single-axis G01 move to add a fillet/corner radius. Value = radius size. Sign convention same as chamfer: based on X direction and corner position. Example: G01 X1.0 R0.015 Z-2.0 adds 0.015" blend radius. Works for both internal and external corners.

tips.title: Part zero at finished part end (best practice)
tips.body: Locate Z0 at the end of the finished part, not chuck face. This is the most popular approach for parts machined on both ends: flip part, Z0 stays at the same physical location relative to part features. Makes blueprint dimensions directly programmable without offset math.

tips.title: Gang tooling selection via slide motion
tips.body: Gang tooling mounts multiple tools on the cross slide (no turret). Select tools by explicit X/Z positioning to the desired tool. No T-word tool change — tools are always 'loaded'. Faster for small parts with multiple operations. Requires careful programming to avoid collisions between gang-mounted tools.

tips.title: No M06 on lathes — T-word executes tool change
tips.body: Unlike mills, CNC lathes execute tool changes immediately with the T-word. No M06 required or allowed on most lathe controls. T0200 commands turret rotation to station 2 immediately. Some mill-turn machines use M06; verify your specific control's requirements.
